headline: Last session: Indian benchmark indices snapped two-week gains as surging crude oil prices dragged equities lower.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 26 October.

why: Surging Brent crude oil prices reaching a six-month high pressured Indian shares into weekly losses.
Profit booking across broader equities snapped two consecutive weeks of market gains.
Global cues and rising energy costs weighed negatively on investor sentiment.
IT sector buying offered temporary support but was insufficient to reverse overall market declines.
whatHappening: Nifty closed around 22,600 while Sensex extended losses in the last trading session.
SEBI Chairman announced plans to introduce rules aimed at preventing broker terminal misuse.
Air India suspended flights to Riyadh and Dammam until November 7, impacting international services.
Indian stock markets remain closed on Sunday and will resume trading on Monday, 26 October.
summary: In the last trading session, Indian equity markets snapped a two-week winning streak as surging crude oil prices triggered widespread selling. While buying in IT stocks provided brief resistance, benchmark indices ended lower. Markets are closed today for the weekend and will reopen on Monday, 26 October.
